validity.recommendation: no merge -- P6897 and P4454 are distinct, correctly separate rows
validity.researcher_notes: Compared against P4454 (Ohio Valley Connector Expansion Project / OVCX, FERC docket CP22-44; read that already-complete shard in full for cross-reference, not edited, per scope). P6897 is the ORIGINAL Ohio Valley Connector project: FERC docket CP15-41, application filed by Equitrans, L.P. on 2014-12-30, in service 2016-10-01, a lateral connecting Appalachian Basin (Marcellus/Utica) supply gathered in Wetzel, Marshall and Marion Counties, WV to Rockies Express Pipeline (REX) and Texas Eastern Transmission (TETCO) interconnects at Monroe County, OH, via the Corona (WV) and Plasma (OH) compressor stations. P4454/OVCX is a SEPARATE, later (filed 2022, docket CP22-44) compression-plus-partial-repipe expansion of that same Corona/Plasma corridor. OVCX's own FERC notice of application makes the relationship explicit: 'This Project is an expansion of the Equitrans' Ohio Valley Connector Project which was approved in Docket No. CP15-41-000 and which is already in service' (FR-2022-02-17, 2022-03424). EIA independently tracks these as two distinct project records (row 827 = 'Ohio Valley Connector', docket CP15-41; a separate row = the OVCX project, docket CP22-44) -- two distinct, independent publishers (FERC/Federal Register and EIA) agree these are not the same project. P6897 is not a duplicate of P4454 or vice versa; P4454 is P6897's later, dependent expansion, correctly tracked as its own row. No sheet edit needed; recorded per orchestrator direction.

validity.recommendation: correct Capacity from 4400.00 to 850.00 MMcf/d; CapacityUnits (MMcf/d) is already correct
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet records Capacity=4400.00 MMcf/d with a blank Length/Diameter and an investor-deck ref that 403'd on re-check. Every independent primary source instead states OVC's own designed capacity as 850 MMcf/d (850,000 Dth/d): EIA row 827 'Additional Capacity (MMcf/d) = 850' (stable across all 28 tracked releases 2018-05..2026-08); FERC's original notice of application (FR-2015-01-13, 2015-00311) -- 'The project will provide up to 850,000 dekatherms per day of additional firm transportation service'; and FERC's 2015 amendment notice (FR-2015-05-18, 2015-11921) -- 'The amendment does not affect the Ohio Valley Connector Project's designed capacity of 850 MMcf/day.' Two independent, distinct-publisher origins (EIA + FERC/Federal Register) agree on 850, not 4,400. LIKELY ORIGIN OF THE ERROR: Equitrans Midstream Corporation's own 'Transmission' web page (Wayback-captured 2026-01-13, http://web.archive.org/web/20260113022337/https://www.equitransmidstream.com/transmission/ -- not cited as a proposed_ref here because it does not name 'Ohio Valley Connector' specifically and so fails the --name check) states that, as of 2022-12-31, Equitrans' ENTIRE ~940-mile FERC-regulated transmission-and-storage SYSTEM (all lines combined) has 'total throughput capacity of approximately 4.4 Bcf per day' -- i.e. 4,400 MMcf/d is a real, correctly-sourced figure, but it describes the whole multi-pipeline Equitrans system, not any single segment. This is almost certainly how 4,400 ended up recorded on this row (and, per the orchestrator's brief, apparently on sibling rows P6895 and P6896 as well, both also showing 4400.00 MMcf/d with blank endpoints) -- a system-level aggregate figure copied onto individual segment rows. See cross_row_leads for P6895/P6896.

fills.researcher_notes: Cell was blank (MISSING_VALUE). Single strong origin (EIA), stable across 8 years / 28 releases. FERC's original Sept 2014 pre-filing scope (FR-2014-09-08, 2014-21206) corroborates both diameters were part of the initial engineering design: ~34 mi/30-in mainline (H-310) + 1.5 mi/30-in tie-in (H-311) + 14 mi/24-in loop (H-313) + 0.6 mi/16-in discharge (H-306). However, FERC's May 2015 amendment (FR-2015-05-18, 2015-11921) formally REMOVED the 14-mile, 24-inch H-313 loop from project scope before construction ('Equitrans proposes to eliminate the H-313 pipeline from the scope of the project'), while stating capacity was unaffected. Despite that removal, EIA's diameter field has read a 24-in/30-in pair in every one of 28 releases spanning 2018-2026, well after the amendment -- either a different 24-inch segment was retained/added elsewhere in the as-built design, or EIA's field simply was not updated for the 2015 scope change. Flagging this tension rather than silently resolving it; kept at medium (not high) because of it, and not raised as a validity concern since the sheet's own cell was blank (no existing wrong value to correct here).

P6897's own true segment capacity is 850 MMcf/d (EIA row 827 + FERC docket CP15-41). Recommend whoever holds P6895 verify that segment's own true capacity independently rather than inherit this system-wide figure; not resolved here, per scope.

P6896 ('Allenghy'/Allegheny Valley Connector) reads the identical Capacity=4400.00 MMcf/d defect (see the P6895 lead for the likely system-wide-figure origin). Separately, this SEC 8-K (EQT Midstream Partners LP, Q3 2016) states AVC was ACQUIRED via a December 2013 capital lease from EQT Corporation, not newly constructed: 'In December 2013, EQM entered into a capital lease with EQT Corporation (EQT) for the Allegheny Valley Connector facilities (AVC) ... Relevant corporate-history/attribution context for whoever holds P6896; not resolved here, per scope.
